newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL POWER TO DRAW $86 BLN IN INVESTMENT BY 2000.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL POWER TO DRAW $86 BLN IN INVESTMENT BY 2000.

text.p: The Brazilian power sector will draw $85.7 billion of the total $189.9 billion in infrastructure investment expected in the country by the year 2000, an industry group said.
The Brazilian Infrastructure and Basic Industry Association (Abdib) said in a statement that private capital investment will account for $23.8 billion of the expected power-sector investment.

Abdib said its Infra 11 semesterly survey has identified 557 electrical projects planned in Brazil by the year 2000 with power generation accounting for $61.7 billion, distribution $14 billion and transmission $9.8 billion, it added.
"Since the last report in December 1996 there was a 64 percent increase in value of investment and 22 percent (increase) in the number of projects," the statement said.
Generation projects now underway total $9.4 billion to build 36 power plants, including 17 private projects worth $608 million, it said.
